clue.text: Treacherous person upended Scotsman's stuff on the road

indicators.note: turned end over end, so the word for the traitor is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer
Mac is a familiar way to address a Scotsman, and the 's attaches it

explanation.surface: A traitor turns over a Scot's belongings left lying in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff on the road' is the definition: the surfacing material, not someone's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the asphalt-and-stone material used to surface roads.

clue.text: This list should show the fare for Paris

definitions.text: This list should show the fare for Paris

parts.words: This list should show the fare for Paris
parts.note: a menu listing dishes individually priced, a French phrase, so it is the bill of fare one would see in Paris

explanation.surface: A train timetable ought to display the ticket price to the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a travel ticket; it is food, and the list is a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means ordering from the menu dish by dish, each separately priced.

clue.text: One makes a killing twice regarding instrument that's beaten up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom, backwards
the word for regarding is given two times

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
a drum is a percussion instrument, beaten when played

explanation.surface: A businessperson profits handsomely from a percussion instrument being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten up' fits the drum, but signals reversal of the whole string RE RE DRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a killing is the idiom for big profit; literally, a killer commits one.

clue.text: Firm with politician within the law, but sharing guilt

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
MP is a Member of Parliament
licit means lawful

explanation.surface: A company and an MP act legally, yet both are to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Being complicit means being involved with others in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Inflates benefits to include everybody

indicators.note: one word's letters are made to include another's, holding it inside

parts.note: boons are blessings or benefits
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A claim that welfare payments swell when extended to all.
explanation.definitionFit: To balloon is to swell rapidly, as a verb meaning grows or puffs up.

clue.text: Posterior and chest seen, sadly in secret

parts.note: behind is a word for the backside

indicators.note: the words are in a sorry state, so their letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: An embarrassing exposure of backside and torso, regrettably out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Done out of public view, as theatre work happens away from the stage.

clue.text: Liberal European circle supports end of inane ogling

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the others
the final letter of the word inane

parts.note: a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: A political group's circle backs some silly staring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogling is staring lecherously, much the same as a lustful sidelong look.

clue.text: Little work of note?

parts.note: an opera is a work made of musical notes, and the diminutive form is a short light one

explanation.surface: Asks about a minor but distinguished piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' seems to mean notable; it means made of musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, light opera with spoken dialogue, literally 'little opera' in Italian.

clue.text: Inactive sort of party needing new worker

parts.note: a stag party is a groom's pre-wedding celebration
a worker ant, the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A sluggish celebration that needs a fresh hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant means not flowing or developing, hence still and inactive.

clue.text: Mostly firm rear — hard to express disapproval!

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter cut off

parts.note: hard means firm or solid
the rump is the hindquarters
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A grumble about a toughened backside, ending in an exclamation of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' and 'hard' are both used, the first trimmed to HAR, the second abbreviated to H.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to make a gruff throat-clearing noise showing displeasure.

clue.text: High-ranking officer dismissing line in groups

indicators.note: the officer sends away one letter, so it is removed

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A senior officer discharges a soldier from the ranks of several units.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are taxonomic classes, plural of genus, so they are groups of related species.

clue.text: Navigator chap welcomes legal wrangling

indicators.note: the word for a fellow takes the other letters in, holding them inside

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: argument churns the letters of the word legal around

explanation.surface: A seafarer gladly receives some lawyerly squabbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand Magellan was the Portuguese explorer whose expedition first sailed round the world.

clue.text: Glutton needing long time to get responsibility

parts.note: a greedy eater is called a pig
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A greedy eater takes ages before accepting a duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the idiom 'that's not my pigeon', meaning not my concern.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British idiom 'not my pigeon', the bird stands for one's own business or concern.

clue.text: Dramatic summoning by old flame

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
citing means summoning before a court

explanation.surface: A former lover is hauled into court, causing a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrilling or full of suspense is dramatic, a close synonym.

clue.text: Proposed to show agreement with poor inmate locked in

indicators.note: the shuffled prisoner is shut inside the nod

parts.note: to nod is to signal agreement

indicators.note: a poor version of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A suggestion agreed to with a needy prisoner shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominated means put forward as a candidate, so proposed.

clue.text: Sort of hug stomach?

definitions.meaning: to stomach something is to tolerate or put up with it

explanation.surface: A query whether an embrace might be called a tummy hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear names a crushing embrace and also means to endure, as in cannot stand it.

clue.text: Times grabs a couple of students who heard commotion

indicators.note: the word for times seizes the letters and holds them inside

parts.note: by means times, as in three by four
L is a learner or student, so two of them are LL

indicators.note: the word who as spoken aloud, spelt differently

parts.note: said aloud, who sounds like hoo

explanation.surface: A newspaper seizes two pupils who overheard a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but multiplication, as in 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy fuss or sensational publicity.

clue.text: Financial check covering account year — that's daring

indicators.note: the check wraps itself around the other letters

parts.note: an audit is an inspection of accounts

explanation.surface: An accountant boldly reviews the year's books.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity is boldness or daring, sometimes shading into cheek.

clue.text: Diplomatic approach sees bill on time

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a parliamentary bill becomes an act when passed

explanation.surface: Tactfully presenting the account at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact is skill in handling people sensitively, the essence of diplomacy.

clue.text: Discharge business coaches with one missing turn

indicators.note: the coaches are lacking a letter, which is removed

parts.note: to coach is to train, so coaches is trains
one is the Roman numeral I
an act is a turn on stage

explanation.surface: A sports trainer, short one player, takes a turn at handling the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to conduct or carry out a deal, as discharging business.

clue.text: Greek island fires cavalry

parts.note: Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: An island in Greece dismisses its mounted troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were Russian and Ukrainian horsemen famed as light cavalry.

clue.text: Flag of current Queen

parts.note: a stream is a flow or current of water
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The royal standard of the present monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present-day', but it is the flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant flying from a mast.

clue.text: Snobbish — and mystified at university

parts.note: stuck means baffled, unable to proceed
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A haughty student baffled by college life.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck-up is informal for arrogantly superior or conceited.

clue.text: The French will get fit for this sporting competition

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: The French players get in shape for a sports championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' suggests healthy, but it is a noun: a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a group of clubs competing against each other over a season.

clue.text: Church must accept shortly one's to make saint

indicators.note: the church abbreviation has to take the other letters into itself

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
anon means soon or shortly
one is I, and the 's is S

explanation.surface: The church must soon agree to give someone sainthood.
explanation.definitionFit: To canonise is formally to declare a dead person a saint.

clue.text: Gives a lift to American country folk full of love?

indicators.note: the rustics contain the other letter inside them

parts.note: hicks are unsophisticated rural people in American slang
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Romantic rural Americans offer someone a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoick is to lift or haul something up abruptly, a British informal verb.

clue.text: Little songbird making teachers brood?

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers
a hatch is a brood of young produced at one time

explanation.surface: A small bird makes schoolteachers sit and sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' reads as a verb for sulking, but here it is the noun for a batch of chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland bird that climbs tree trunks and sings.

clue.text: Sporting meet worried slimy cop

indicators.note: worried in the sense of shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: An oily policeman is anxious about a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympics is the international multi-sport gathering held every four years.

clue.text: Feel an aversion towards international following first couple of defeats

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer
the opening two letters of the word defeats are taken

parts.note: a test is an international match, as in Test cricket

explanation.surface: A player hates an international match after starting with two losses.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe or hate intensely.
